name: Sagittarius Dwarf Galaxy
tagline: The Milky Way's nearest known satellite — a spheroid already being torn into star streams as it falls through the disc.

facts.label: Fate
facts.value: Being disrupted; star streams wrap the galaxy

history: The Sagittarius Dwarf Spheroidal Galaxy was only noticed in 1994, hidden on the far side of the galactic centre behind the Milky Way's own stars. It is being shredded: tidal tails of its stars arc hundreds of thousands of light-years around the galaxy, and its globular cluster M54 may mark what remains of its core. Its ongoing disintegration is a live demonstration of how large galaxies grow by consuming smaller ones.
source: Sloan Digital Sky Survey · Ibata et al.
